newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia still talks with Germans over gas selloff.
newsitem.headline: Latvia still talks with Germans over gas selloff.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) on Monday said it was still in talks with Preussen and Ruhrgas on the privatiation of Latvian Gas, on which the German companies have to make a decision in two weeks.

Preussen and Ruhrgas formed a consortium to buy a stake in Latvian Gas. Russia's Gazprom is taking part as a separate partner. The German firms are concerned about Latvian Gas' large debts and have sought government guarantees.
"The Germans have asked the Latvian side for a few explanations on the agreeement's legal aspects, like from which date dividends are calculated," an LPA official told Reuters.
"Legally, the Germans have the right to announce their decision by the afternoon of February 14," the official added.
The Latvian side has offered to guarantee some of the debts but not all.
French state-owned Gaz de France may be offered the stake in Latvian Gas if the German firms pull out, the LPA has said.
The official would not give details on the prospects of Gaz de France taking part in the sale but said that relations were "friendly and neutral".
